role: Operator runbook for production incidents: per-category symptoms and actions (AI provider outage, CloudKit failure, crash spike, encryption key loss, HealthKit data errors, privacy leak suspicion, transitive-dependency CVE) plus a post-incident note template.
toplevel: Markdown only; no executable content. References code symbols (FeatureFlags, EncryptionManager.getOrCreateKey/keychainAccount/reEncryptIfNeeded, CloudPayloadCodec, SleepBoundaryResolver, AppFactResolver, ProviderConsentTracker), the make target sendable-guard, docs/runbooks/hotfix.md, .github/dependabot.yml open-pull-requests-limit and the iCloud container iCloud.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery; all of these exist in the repo (Constants.swift:12, Emuqu.entitlements:23, Makefile:58, .github/dependabot.yml:24).

units.does: no behavioural claim: title and preamble telling the operator to pick the matching section.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > A. AI provider outage / breaking change
units.does: Claims the per-provider kill switch lives in FeatureFlags (Settings -> Flo), is per-device with no remote config, so a provider can be disabled for everyone only by shipping a build, and that changing the default is not enough because FeatureFlags.value(for:) returns a stored value over defaultValue and the Settings toggle stores an explicit Bool on every flip, so the build must also ignore or clear the stored key or disable the provider in code; providers live in Sources/Assistant/Providers/ and implement a small AIProvider protocol. Code matches: FeatureFlags.value(for:)/set(_:for:) (Constants+SleepAndDisplay.swift:402-420), AIAssistantSettingsPage.bindingFor(flag:) setter calls set.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > B. CloudKit sync failure (zone-wide)
units.does: CloudKit outage triage: check CloudKit Dashboard for container iCloud.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery, deploy schema to production if only this container fails, never mass-reset user state. Container id matches Constants.swift:12 and Emuqu.entitlements:23; schema-not-deployed failure mode is the one CloudKitSessionFreshness.noteSaveFailure logs ("not in the production schema").

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > C. Crash spike
units.does: Crash-spike triage: symbolicate from App Store Connect/dSYM, read code at the crashing line, run make sendable-guard, hotfix via hotfix.md. make sendable-guard exists (Makefile:58) and docs/runbooks/hotfix.md exists. Listed common causes are prose, not tied to code.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > D. Encryption key loss
units.does: Encryption key loss triage: device not unlocked since reboot (archive key is AfterFirstUnlock), iCloud Keychain sync of the synchronizable CloudPayloadCodec key (one Keychain item per key; log line 'waiting for its backup key to sync'), restore without Keychain loses the archive key, then Delete All My Data (type DELETE MY DATA). For wide-scale failures inspect EncryptionManager.getOrCreateKey(version:), keychainAccount(for:) per version, and add a previous-version fallback modeled on reEncryptIfNeeded. Code: accessibility kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock (EncryptionManager.swift:252), per-key accounts 'cloud-payload-key-id-' (CloudPayloadCodec.swift:76), log line at CloudKitSyncManager+Pull.swift:305, confirm phrase at DeleteAllDataPage.swift:28.

flags.text: Step 3-4 says a key-version bump without migration makes old files unreadable and that a hotfix must add a fallback to try the previous key version. decrypt already reads the version byte from each blob and loads that version's key (EncryptionManager.swift:99-106, extractVersion :148, loadKey :188), so old files stay readable as long as the old Keychain item exists; decryption does not go through getOrCreateKey at all. reEncryptIfNeeded has no caller (comment EncryptionManager.swift:25-27). An operator following the runbook would look for the wrong failure mechanism.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > E. Apple Health data corruption
units.does: HealthKit data-corruption triage: suspect DST/time-zone math in SleepBoundaryResolver and addingTimeInterval patterns, reproduce with the user's date, hotfix with a regression test. SleepBoundaryResolver exists (Emuqu/Sources/Analysis/SleepBoundaryResolver.swift:52).

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > F. Privacy / leak suspicion
units.does: Privacy-leak triage: treat as P0; verify AppFactResolver sends only aggregates; verify ProviderConsentTracker gates provider calls; step 4 says the exported diagnostic log cannot show what was sent (PHI-scrubbed, no payloads) and points to LLMRequestAudit (last 10 chat-loop requests, in memory, lost on quit; summaries, fact extraction and voice interjections not recorded), read via Troubleshooting with Advanced Diagnostics on -> AI prompt audit and shared from the detail screen; if real, ship a build that turns the provider off, noting a default-off flag alone is not enough because a stored value wins, then update SECURITY.md. Code: LLMRequestAudit maxEntries 10, not persisted (LLMRequestAudit.swift:3-31); the audit section shows only with debugModeEnabled (SettingsPages+Diagnostics.swift:67-75); LLMPromptAuditDetailView has a ShareLink; DebugLogger.scrubPHI; FeatureFlags.value(for:) prefers the stored value.

flags.text: Step 5 says 'File a SECURITY.md update'; there is no SECURITY.md at the repository root, only .github/SECURITY.md, so the instruction names a file location that does not exist as written.

units.key: § Runbook: Incident Response > G. CVE against a transitive dependency you cannot bump
units.does: Transitive-dependency CVE playbook: Zip and swift-protobuf arrive via polar-ble-sdk (BLE sensor path), yyjson and the other swift-* packages via WhisperKit (voice path), the same split scripts/generate_sbom.py records (DIRECT comment, generate_sbom.py:32-35); establish reachability, ship a build with the path off (no runtime flag for the sensor path; voice degrades to typed input), file upstream, bump by hand because Dependabot open-pull-requests-limit: 0 blocks version PRs only. Package.resolved lists polar-ble-sdk, whisperkit, yyjson, zip, swift-protobuf and other swift-* packages.

flags.text: Runbook says that with the WhisperKit path off, voice degrades to typed input. In code WhisperKit is an opt-in STT provider; Apple SFSpeechRecognizer is the default and the documented fallback when WhisperKit fails to load or transcribe, and non-English locales already route to Apple. Turning the WhisperKit path off leaves voice working via Apple Speech, so the user-facing message the runbook prescribes overstates the loss.

units.does: no behavioural claim: post-incident note template (what broke, detection time, root cause, why CI missed it, prevention, TTD/TTM/TTF).
